gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-meroiti: Junegull draws every line as if traced with one marker tip, pinched at the mouth of each curve and chunky as cast iron. Noto Sans Meroitic goes down easily beneath it.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-mono: Junegull brings a retro, friendly swagger, its curves pinched shut like cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Mono replies with generously spaced, sturdy lowercase, and that open-versus-closed tension is the pair's real pull.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-mro: Noto Sans Mro looks dense and tall through the middle of every word. Junegull up top keeps its strokes unshaded and its curves pinched, so the two share a blunt, modern confidence.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-multani: Wire-like and wide-eyed. Junegull's tubular letters sit above Noto Sans Multani, whose lofty x-height and gapped e give it lift, and a slightly larger body size would let that openness show.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Noto Sans Myanmar forms a thick, heavy-looking band of text with broad openings. Junegull above it keeps one unvarying stroke thickness and pinched curves, so a touch more body size would help the text breathe.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-nabatae: Retro and friendly, Junegull holds a tube-like thickness through every bend and closes its curves tight. And Noto Sans Nabataean, with near cap-tall lowercase and wide-open s curves, makes that closed-versus-open difference the pair's best quality.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-nag-mun: Noto Sans Nag Mundari has half-unwrapped curves and lowercase that rivals capitals. Junegull's spaghetti-like line stays closed and pinched above it, and that tight-against-open contrast is the strongest thing here.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-nandina: Noto Sans Nandinagari keeps generous openings at every weight, with short ascenders and a big lowercase body. And Junegull's plain, unshaded line never swells, so enlarging the body text a little lets that friendly openness carry.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-newa: Noto Sans Newa leaves the mouth of its lowercase e clearly open, with tall counters and bowls throughout. Junegull draws chunky closed shapes; Newa keeps the reading easy.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Junegull is retro and friendly, with pinched curves and a lowercase as stout as cast iron capitals. And Noto Sans Nushu, with its towering x-height and far-flung terminals, would feel lost if the heading were made small.
